summary: Luke Badiali ran a session with Simon Clarke and Priya Natarajan on expanding work across portfolio companies and funds. Most 100-day plans end at day 100 with no follow-on. We agreed a post-plan advisory retainer and quarterly reviews with the top funds.

discussion.keyPoints: Simon said only 3 of the last 14 portfolio companies bought anything after the plan. Priya felt CIOs want help with delivery oversight but nobody offers it.
Four funds account for 55% of revenue. Priya meets their deal partners often but rarely their operating partners.
There is no formal feedback after DD or 100-day plans. Simon was keen but worried about survey fatigue among deal teams.

recommendations.recommendation: Offer a 9-month delivery assurance retainer at 8,000 GBP per month at day 80 of every 100-day plan.
Treat the 4 funds that make up 55% of revenue as key accounts with a quarterly review including the operating partner.
Ask for a 3-question rating after each DD readout.
Ask portfolio CEOs for a reference call within 90 days of the plan ending.
Run a formal onboarding pack for each new portfolio company.

actions.action: Draft the delivery assurance retainer scope and day-80 conversation guide
Book quarterly reviews with the 4 key account funds

nextFocus: Model the economics of DD, 100-day plans and the delivery assurance retainer.
nextPreparation: Simon to bring utilisation, day rates and margin by service line for the last 12 months.

tests.question: What did we agree to offer after the 100-day plan?
What did we agree about key account funds?
Is the rating after each DD readout agreed?
